Working from the article text provided directly. Here is the analysis:

Published online:
    September 4, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Japan, United States, Global (G20)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — References 1998 LTCM, April–May intervention, July–August coordinated action
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — BOJ September/October hike odds, carry trade unwind, JPY repatriation flows
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — Structural yen revaluation, GPIF domestic pivot, JPY short unwind toward 142–146 range

Synopsis:
    The yen is reversing a multi-year bearish trend driven by converging forces: near-certain BOJ rate hike expectations (25bps in September, 97% probability), growing speculation of faster/larger hikes (50bps floated), U.S. political pressure from Treasury Secretary Bessent, domestic capital repatriation led by institutional investors unwinding foreign bond positions, and carry trade deleveraging. JPY positioning has flipped net-long. A full unwind of ~¥17 trillion in shorts could push USD/JPY to 142–146. On the U.S. side, dovish Fed commentary (Waller) is trimming rate-hike expectations, narrowing the rate differential that has driven yen weakness.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: NO — The primary focus is JPY dynamics and BOJ policy. The Fed and U.S. rates appear as a secondary, supporting factor explaining the rate differential driving yen weakness/recovery.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 5 (strongly NO — the Fed angle is about potential cuts/dovish pivot, not hikes)
Probability of increase: ~5%

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 30 (partially — the Fed is in the background; no explicit hold decision discussed, but no cut is confirmed either)
Probability of holding: ~40%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 55 (the Waller dovish comments driving "trimmed expectations for a U.S. rate increase" implies the market leans toward cuts or at minimum no hike, which narrows the BOJ/Fed spread)
Probability of decrease: ~55%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: -65 (Meaningfully more dovish than before — Waller's dovish comments explicitly caused traders to trim U.S. rate hike expectations, reinforcing the rate differential compression narrative that is accelerating the yen recovery and carry trade unwind)
